topics: Control plane vs data plane separation
Ingress and egress firewalling and NAT/PrivateLink
Audit logs, SIEM integration, retention and tamper-resistance
Encryption at-rest with AWS KMS / BYOK and HSM options
questions: How does Redwood separate customer control plane metadata from data plane?
Can we BYOK with our HSM and keep keys in our account?
How are egress flows minimized and what mandatory outbound endpoints does Redwood require?
What's the expected audit log volume and retention options?
Does Redwood support SCIM for provisioning and RBAC role sync?
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SA), Priya Shah (Horizon Head of Security), Marcus Lee (Cloud Engineer), Dana Park (CISO), Oliver Ng (Compliance)

Summary (auto): deep dive on Private/VPC deployment and security controls. Customer wants specifics on network isolation, ingress/egress, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and KMS/BYOK.

00:00 Alicia Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we know folks are on a tight timeline so we'll focus on the network and the security controls for Redwood Private in your VPC. Diego will walk the data plane layout, and Samir will cover keys and audit flows.
00:19 Priya Shah: thanks Alicia, yeah we are especially interested in egress containment and how much outbound connectivity we need to allow, and also the BYOK story for keys.
00:34 Diego Morales: cool, so at a high level Redwood Private splits the control plane and data plane, control plane remains in Redwood-managed cloud unless you choose fully air-gapped on-prem, while the data plane—the inference workers—run in your VPC. so you get local networking and storage. sorry, that was a mouthful.
00:58 Marcus Lee: when you say control plane remains with Redwood, what metadata crosses the wire? we can't have inference payloads leaving our network.
01:09 Diego Morales: good question. the control plane only receives orchestration signals and metrics; the actual model inputs and outputs stay on the data plane. that said we can provide an option to route control plane traffic over an S2S VPN or PrivateLink to reduce exposure. transcript note: sometimes we say K V cash instead of KV cache in the call.
01:38 Dana Park: is there an option to run the control plane in our environment? some banks require the whole control plane internal.
01:48 Samir Patel: yes, for full air-gapped deployments we can offer a private control plane package—it's a heavier lift (on-prem or VPC-hosted control plane), additional license and professional services. many customers start with control plane in Redwood and then move to private control plane if required.
02:10 Priya Shah: can you walk through ingress? we have strict inbound rules.
02:17 Diego Morales: ingress is via a bastion/proxy pattern. you can deploy a small nat/bastion that fronts the inference fleet; we also support internal load balancers and PrivateLink endpoints for the control signals. for user traffic you can use an ALB/NLB in front of the pods with strict SGs. the main idea is to keep all data-plane interfaces private.
02:45 Marcus Lee: what about egress to pull models or telemetry? we have denied internet egress except for approved endpoints.
02:52 Samir Patel: right, so minimal egress is required. we publish a short list of endpoints for metrics, license checks, and optional model downloads. In Private VPC we recommend preloading model artifacts into an S3 bucket in your account or using a private registry so you avoid outbound pulls. for telemetry you can push logs to customer SIEM via VPC endpoints.
03:22 Priya Shah: so you can do BYOModels and BYOK? we do not want artifacts from outside.
03:29 Diego Morales: yes BYO for both models and keys. models can be staged in your artifact repo. keys: we integrate with AWS KMS and support BYOK where you keep keys in your account and grant the Redwood data-plane role access. we also support Azure Key Vault and GCP KMS. for HSM-backed keys we have a couple of customers using HSM in their account.
03:55 Oliver Ng: what about tamper-evidence on logs? we need immutability and chain-of-custody for audit.
04:02 Samir Patel: we forward audit logs to your SIEM (Splunk, SumoLogic, Datadog, or direct to S3) with signed timestamps; customers often enable S3 Object Lock for retention/immutability. we can also stream to an external collector over TLS with mTLS.
04:30 Marcus Lee: what sort of latency does Private add? just curious.
04:35 Diego Morales: depends on network topology; inside the same region it's low single-digit ms for model server hops; the bigger overhead is inter-subnet routing and your firewall rules. in practice customers see similar P99 as hosted but attach variability if packet inspection/IDS is inline.
04:56 Priya Shah: ok can you show me a sample VPC diagram?
05:01 Diego Morales: sure. I'll put one in the follow-up, but quick voice diagram: public subnet for bastion and jump, private subnet(s) for inference workers, private S3 endpoints for model/artifact pulls, private route tables with no IGW on worker subnets, NAT only for controlled egress, or prefer VPC endpoints to keep egress inside the cloud.
05:28 Priya Shah: do you require NAT? we try to avoid NAT gateway costs and egress to internet altogether.
05:33 Samir Patel: you do not need a NAT if you stage everything in the VPC and use interface endpoints. the only time NAT is required is for outbound access to third-party endpoints. we recommend using Gateway/Interface endpoints for S3 and KMS.
05:52 Marcus Lee: can we do PrivateLink to Redwood for the control plane so we never touch public internet?
05:58 Diego Morales: yes PrivateLink is supported for control-plane connectivity; control plane signals then go over the interface endpoint. for some customers we also establish a managed VPN or Direct Connect.
06:15 Dana Park: RBAC and provisioning: we need SCIM + SAML and role sync to our IdP. we also want least privilege.
06:26 Samir Patel: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, with RBAC roles you can map to groups. we also integrate with Okta, Azure AD. you can restrict API keys and provide route-level permissions; we also have token scoping. small caveat: some older SDKs might still use API keys but new flows prefer short-lived tokens via your IdP.
06:54 Priya Shah: are API calls from the app to the data plane authenticated with mTLS or bearer tokens?
07:00 Diego Morales: the data plane enforces mTLS for inter-service communications and optional mTLS for client connections. most customers use short-lived bearer tokens that the control plane mints, but for our highest security customers we support client certs.
07:20 Oliver Ng: about audit logs again—what's in the logs? full prompt content? we have data governance concerns over PII in prompts.
07:31 Samir Patel: by default you can choose to redact prompts from persisted logs. Redwood has a config to disable storing raw prompts and only store hashes/metadata for auditing. if you need full fidelity for compliance, we'd recommend encrypting logs with your KMS key and forwarding to your SIEM.
07:58 Priya Shah: interesting. what's the default retention window?
08:03 Alicia Chen: typical default is 90 days in the hosted product but in Private you can set retention to match policy and export to S3 with longer retention. many banks set 7 years in immutable S3 buckets.
08:17 Marcus Lee: when you say encrypt logs with our KMS key, is that customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed?
08:23 Samir Patel: you can do customer-managed KMS (BYOK). the data plane will request DEKs encrypted with your CMK. Redwood never has plaintext of the CMK. for the key rotation and policy we rely on your KMS policies.
08:40 Dana Park: is there any metadata that still leaves the VPC? like usage metering?
08:46 Diego Morales: metering/usage is optional: you can push metrics aggregates to the control plane, or you can keep raw metrics in your account and opt out of usage telemetry. we do require some minimal heartbeat for service health, which can be routed over PrivateLink if desired.
09:06 Priya Shah: what about compliance artifacts—do you provide SOC2 Type II report details and ISO certification?
09:12 Alicia Chen: yes we'll share our SOC2 and ISO 27001 cert and the pen-test summary. again for a private deployment we can include additional attestation as part of the enterprise contract. I'll send the package after the call.
09:28 Priya Shah: great. can you describe the ingress TLS termination model? we terminate in the VPC or at the ALB?
09:36 Diego Morales: termination is configurable. many customers terminate TLS at their ALB and then use mTLS to talk to pods, or do end-to-end TLS using passthrough with client certs to the pod. it's flexible.
09:52 Marcus Lee: firewalling: do you need wide outbound ports? we run strict egress rules only to our CIDRs.
09:57 Samir Patel: Redwood recommends specific egress ports for NTP, CRL/OCSP if you use cert checks, and endpoints for KMS and S3. but if you host KMS and S3 in same account we can avoid public egress. we'll provide a minimal allowed ports list—usually HTTPS 443 and some ephemeral for health checks.
10:23 Priya Shah: what's your recommended approach for private model downloads during deployment?
10:28 Diego Morales: recommend preloading and versioning models in customer-owned S3, then the data plane pulls from that S3 via an instance role. optionally, you can use an internal artifact registry with VPC endpoints. avoid public download at runtime.
10:45 Oliver Ng: how about vulnerability management for the data plane images? we need CVE scanning and image provenance.
10:51 Samir Patel: images are signed and provenance is recorded; we run regular CVE scans and provide SBOMs on request. can provide attested images or allow you to build images with our base and run in your pipeline.
11:10 Dana Park: for on-prem and air-gapped how do you handle model updates and patches?
11:16 Diego Morales: that's slower process: we provide signed bundles that you can import via secure media or an approved internal artifact pipeline. we also offer a managed update pipeline with offline sync for air-gapped customers.
11:33 Priya Shah: any recommendations around packet inspection/IDS? we use an inline IDS that might add latency.
11:38 Diego Morales: inline DPI will add overhead; we recommend placing IDS at network boundaries and using mirroring for deep inspection rather than inline for latency-sensitive inference flows. also use sampling for high-throughput logs.
11:58 Marcus Lee: can you talk about key rotation and compromise procedures for BYOK? what happens if a CMK is revoked?
12:05 Samir Patel: if a CMK is rotated or revoked, you need to coordinate with Redwood to re-encrypt DEKs and rotate the wrapping. we recommend a staged rotation approach: create new CMK, rotate DEKs, test on small subset, then cutover. in worst-case compromise we can stop using the key and re-encrypt artifacts to a new key. we'll support your incident response runbook.
12:33 Priya Shah: how does logging handle redaction? can we have rules to scrub PII from prompts before they hit logs?
12:40 Samir Patel: yes that's configurable. we offer server-side scrubbing with regex-based rules and a pipeline to remove or hash sensitive fields prior to storage. you can also do client-side scrubbing if you want no sensitive data sent at all.
13:01 Alicia Chen: quick pause  — wants to recap core asks: 1) egress-minimized deployment using S3 endpoints and PrivateLink, 2) BYOK for KMS and HSM integration, 3) SIEM forwarding and immutable retention, 4) SCIM/SAML RBAC integration, 5) audit log redaction options. is that accurate?
13:25 Priya Shah: yes that's correct. also add sample firewall rules and minimal outbound endpoints.
13:34 Diego Morales: noted; we'll include a sample Security Group and route table snippet in the follow-up.
13:42 Marcus Lee: does Redwood require any specific OS-level ports open on the workers?
13:46 Samir Patel: minimal: health and metrics (from your monitoring account), model server port, and management plane ports for orchestration which can be locked down to the bastion. we'll provide exact port numbers in doc.
13:58 Priya Shah: re: audit trail tamper resistance—any support for append-only log stores or ledger-like storage?
14:06 Samir Patel: customers often forward to S3 with Object Lock or a managed ledger like QLDB if they need tamper-evident ledgering. Redwood can sign records and route them to your ledger.
14:24 Dana Park: any regulatory concerns for data residency? we need EU-data to stay in eu-west region.
14:30 Diego Morales: region pinning is supported; we can keep data plane nodes in specific regions and control plane metadata is also region-aware for some customers. for full compliance we recommend private control plane in the region.
14:49 Priya Shah: what's the standard SLA for private deployments?
14:53 Alicia Chen: SLA depends on tier and reserved capacity; typical enterprise contracts include 99.9% uptime for dedicated pools and support windows. exact numbers we'll provide in the contract.
15:08 Marcus Lee: For the pilot, we'd like to exercise: 1) private VPC deploy, 2) SIEM forwarding to Splunk, 3) BYOK integration, 4) run 1k concurrent small-short prompts to validate tail latencies.
15:22 Alicia Chen: great we'll work with you on the test plan. Diego can provide an infra checklist.
15:31 Oliver Ng: any recommended mitigations for exfil attempts in prompts? we have policies to detect exfil-likely content.
15:38 Samir Patel: we can integrate content filters, warn on PII-like patterns, and enforce redaction. also policy-level rate limiting and anomaly detection in the console.
15:56 Priya Shah: last question: do you have an incident response playbook for data plane breaches?
16:02 Alicia Chen: yes we have an IR playbook; for private deployments it's joint response: you own the VPC and we provide forensic artifacts and playbooks. we'll share a redacted copy of the IR runbook.
16:20 Marcus Lee: ok, that helps. one more—certificate revocation: do you rely on CRL or OCSP?
16:27 Diego Morales: supports both, but OCSP stapling is recommended for performance. if you enforce CRL checks, that will increase egress for CRL endpoints.
16:44 Priya Shah: thanks. can we review a sample IAM policy for the instance role that lets the data plane access S3 and KMS?
16:50 Samir Patel: yes Diego will attach a sample inline policy showing least privilege.
17:01 Alicia Chen: quick recap of deliverables — I'll send SOC2/ISO/pen test and a high-level architecture; Diego will send VPC diagram, SG/route snippets, and sample IAM policy; Samir will include BYOK/HSM integration notes and logging options. Marcus will propose pilot dates.
17:23 Priya Shah: sounds good. thanks everyone.
17:28 Alicia Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot planning and network call.
17:35 (meeting end)
